channel.title: MeNew Soft
channel.description: MeNew Soft (menewsoft.com) builds web pages for small neighbourhood businesses in Korea. Browse listed shops by area and trade, and follow news from the shops we list.

item.title: What It Actually Means to Run a Local LLM on a Mac mini — The M6 and M5 Pro Math
item.description: In August 2026 the Mac mini moved to M6 and M5 Pro, and Apple spent the announcement talking about on-device AI. Here is where the Mac mini is structurally strong for local LLM work, and where the spec sheet hides the traps. The short version: the first number to look at is not GPU cores, it is memory.

item.title: AMD Beat Every Number and Still Fell 5% — What the Quarter Actually Tested
item.description: AMD posted $11.5B in Q2 revenue, doubled its data center business, and guided Q3 above consensus. The stock dropped more than 5% after hours anyway. The problem was never the numbers — it was what the price already assumed. And for Korean memory, the quarter left a signal that matters more than the stock move.

item.title: The Capital Stayed, the Wiring Left: How LINE Actually Passed to Japan
item.description: The common belief that Naver sold its LINE Yahoo stake is false. A Holdings is still split 50-50. Yet authentication systems, data centers, AI models and even the internal collaboration suite have already been severed from Naver. A two-year record of a transfer that moved the plumbing, not the shares.

item.title: Two Weeks After the Ceasefire Collapsed: How the US–Iran War Bills Oil, Stocks, and Prices — In That Order
item.description: War in February, ceasefire in June, collapse on July 8. Hormuz transits fell from 130 ships a day to 9, oil jumped 10% in a day, and Korea's KOSPI hit a circuit breaker. A map of how the five-month US–Iran war charges its costs to the world economy — and the indicators to watch from here.

item.title: No Profitable AI Small Caps, You Say? Here's One — Polaris Office's Signboard and Its Body
item.description: Among loss-riddled AI small caps sits a company earning 9.1 billion won in operating profit and 13.5 billion in net income, trading at a 141 billion won market cap. Except the body behind the profit isn't AI. Dissecting the accounting of Polaris Office — Korea's first office-AI signboard on a body of industrial affiliates.

item.title: The Day After You Miss the National Team: Konan Technology and the Shadow of Sovereign AI
item.description: The moment it was cut from Korea's 'sovereign AI foundation model' final five, the stock lost 31% in sixteen trading days. The rights offering shrank 39% below plan, and second-largest shareholder SKT sat it out. Dissecting Konan Technology — record revenue coexisting with a fourth straight year of losses — and what remains for the losers of the sovereign AI theme.

item.title: The Korean Arm Dream: Reading OpenEdges' IP Business at Its 52-Week Low
item.description: A company that sells chip blueprints instead of chips just landed Korea's first LPDDR6 interface IP license deal. Yet the stock sits pinned to its 52-week low. Testing whether the semiconductor IP model works in Korea, against OpenEdges' own numbers.

item.title: The Wall the FDA Built, the Price the Market Burned: What's Left of VUNO
item.description: A medical AI company with real hospital revenue slipped at the FDA's doorstep, and the stock lost over 60% in three months. What DeepCARS actually is, what an NSE letter means, and the three checkpoints that will decide whether this drawdown was an overreaction.

item.title: Samsung 2nm's Shadow Partner: Why Gaonchips Trades at Half Its High
item.description: The company that actually executes AI chip designs for Samsung's foundry swung to a loss and lost half its market value. An intraday 30% spike on July 10 was gone within two weeks. What a Korean design house really does, and the three things to verify in H2 2026.

item.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 — When the Foldable Becomes AI's Workbench, and the Traps Fold Users Already Know
item.description: The Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra, unveiled at Unpacked 2026, are the first phones to ship Gemini Intelligence. Why AI is genuinely more useful on a big-screen foldable — and the good and bad lessons (battery, heat, cloud dependence) that Fold 7-generation users have already learned the hard way.

item.title: How to Open Excel, Word and PowerPoint Files with No Install and No Sign-up — A Guide to Our 3 Free Browser Office Editors
item.description: How to open, edit and re-save XLSX, DOCX and PPTX files right in your browser — with zero server uploads. An honest guide to MeNew Sheet, Write and Show: what they do well and where they stop.

item.title: $725 Billion Is About to Get Audited: What Alphabet, Tesla and Intel's Earnings Actually Test
item.description: Three companies worth over $5 trillion report within 48 hours, and the market has decided this is the first real referendum on AI capital spending at scale. Here are the specific numbers that matter — Alphabet's $175-185B capex guide, Tesla's swing to negative free cash flow, Intel's 39.5% gross margin line — and how to read each outcome.

item.title: Kimi K3 Ran Out of GPUs in 48 Hours — and That Tells You More Than the Benchmarks Did
item.description: Moonshot AI paused new Kimi K3 subscriptions two days after launch because its GPU clusters hit capacity. Read alongside the July 27 open-weights release, Microsoft's reported $600M cost-cutting test, and US export controls, the shutdown looks less like a growing pain and more like the strategy itself. A deep analysis of the causes, the economics, and what happens next.

item.title: Jensen Huang Finally Went to Japan — and the Deals He Signed Reveal How Nvidia Is Splitting Asia
item.description: After skipping Japan on an Asia tour and triggering a 'Japan passing' backlash, Nvidia's CEO spent two days in Tokyo and left with a $6.2 billion national AI factory, robotics partnerships with Fanuc and Yaskawa, and a 30-year debt repaid to Sega. What the announcements actually say about the roles Nvidia has assigned to Japan, Korea and Taiwan.

item.title: The Iran War Just Got Worse — So Why Do Global Markets Look Almost Bored?
item.description: Iran has suspended its ceasefire commitments, US strikes have hit a ninth consecutive night, and a war now nearly five months old just entered its most intense phase yet. Yet US futures are up this morning and gold is actually down. Here's what's happening on the ground, what it's done to markets so far, and why the reaction this time looks different.

item.title: Physical AI, Explained Simply: Why It Matters, Who's Winning, and How Good the Robots Actually Are Right Now
item.description: A plain-language primer on 'physical AI' — the industry's name for AI that can perceive and act in the physical world, not just answer text prompts. Why Jensen Huang calls it the next wave after chatbots, who's actually shipping humanoid robots in 2026, and the real state of the technology behind the demos.

item.title: I Let an AI Coding Agent Build Five Browser Games — Here's the Whole Pipeline
item.description: Five real, playable games — a voxel survival game, a kart racer, a match-3 puzzle, a grand-strategy map game, and a platformer — built with an AI coding agent and shipped to a static site with no server, no build step, and no budget. The deployment pattern, the testing trick that made it possible, and the bugs that almost got through.

item.title: Hanwha Aerospace: Riding Europe's Rearmament Boom Into a Premium Valuation
item.description: A howitzer maker that tripled revenue in two years, bought a shipyard, survived a shareholder-rights scandal, and now trades at nearly twice Lockheed Martin's multiple. What the backlog actually buys you, and what it doesn't.

item.title: Kimi K3 Just Pushed Chip Stocks Into a Bear Market — But the Numbers Don't Say What the Headlines Do
item.description: Moonshot AI's 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 sent the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index into an official bear market this week, with traders calling it a DeepSeek repeat. The pricing data tells a different story: this model isn't cheap. Here's what actually happened, and what it does and doesn't mean for the AI capex bet Samsung and SK hynix are riding on.

item.title: Can SK Hynix Rebound? The Question Left by a Roller-Coaster Week
item.description: -12.6%, +8.8%, then -11.5% again. That's SK Hynix's path in four trading days — while its Nasdaq ADR jumped 27%. A one-day rebound built on cooling US inflation was erased in a single session by the 'memory peak-out' narrative. Here's the bull case, the bear case, and the one event that will settle the argument.

item.title: Can Korea's 'AI for Everyone' Compete with GPT, Gemini, and Claude? We Ran the Numbers — and Asked Claude Itself
item.description: Korea's free national AI service will face users who already know GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.1, and Claude. How big is the capability gap, and how real are the Korea-specific advantages? We checked the benchmark data and expert views — then asked Claude (Fable 5), one of the models being compared, for its own honest assessment. Conclusion: the contest won't be decided by general intelligence.

item.title: Free AI for 52 Million People — Inside Korea's 'AI for Everyone' Project
item.description: On July 13, 2026, the Korean government opened the tender for its 'AI for Everyone' project: a free, unlimited AI chatbot for all 52 million citizens by year-end, and a 'one AI agent per citizen' era starting next year. It would make Korea the first G20 nation to do this. Here's how the service is structured, what the conditions reveal, and the five questions that will decide whether it works.

item.title: ASML: The One Company Every AI Chip Must Pass Through
item.description: Every Nvidia GPU and every HBM stack begins inside a machine only one company on Earth can build. What ASML's EUV monopoly actually is, why it is the bedrock layer of AI hardware, and how the stock traveled the AI boom — from a $363 chip-winter low to a $1,768 record.

item.title: Anatomy of a KOSDAQ AI-Theme Spike: The Nable Case Study
item.description: A tiny Korean telecom-software stock hit its 30% daily limit in April with no news, doubled to a 52-week high, then gave it all back. What Nable actually does, what its AI business really is, and what the round trip teaches about Korea's AI-theme trading.

item.title: GPT-5.6 vs. Claude Fable 5: Who Actually Wins the July 2026 Benchmark Wars?
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 both reached general availability within ten days of each other. We break down the actual benchmark numbers — SWE-Bench Pro, TerminalBench, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — plus pricing, context window, and which model wins for which job.

item.title: Why the KOSPI Just Crashed 8% — And What Happens Next
item.description: On July 13, 2026, Korea's KOSPI plunged as much as 9% and triggered its seventh circuit breaker of the year, with SK Hynix down 12% days after a record Nasdaq debut — even as Samsung just posted its best quarter ever. Here's what actually drove the sell-off, and the variables that decide where it goes from here.

item.title: SK Hynix After the Nasdaq Bell: Valuation Re-Rating, Next Moves, and the Risks That Remain
item.description: SK Hynix's record Nasdaq debut is done. Now comes the harder part — whether the premium holds, how it presses its lead over Micron and Samsung, and the value-trap risks analysts are already flagging.

item.title: Can Physical AI Make America a Manufacturing Superpower Again?
item.description: America is building factories at a record pace but can't staff them — nearly 1.9 million jobs may go unfilled by 2033. Physical AI is being sold as the missing worker. Can robots reshore US industry and restore American hegemony? A closer look at the bet, and its hard limits.

item.title: AI Will Do Everything. So What Do I Teach My Kid?
item.description: A developer who watched AI take over rung after rung of his own job asks the parent's version of the question: if machines will do the work, what's actually worth teaching a child? A first-person answer, grounded in what the data on future skills really says.

item.title: SK Hynix's $26.5 Billion Nasdaq Debut: The Biggest Foreign IPO in US History
item.description: SK Hynix just raised $26.5 billion (~40 trillion won) on Nasdaq — the largest US IPO by a foreign company ever, beating Alibaba. And it priced at a premium to Seoul, quietly cracking the Korea Discount. Here's what the record deal means.
